title: Themes
text:
theme() takes a preset and individual options. The presets follow ggplot2’s complete themes:







Preset
Look




vega
Vega-Lite’s defaults


gray (also grey, ggplot2)
gray panel with white grid lines, and ggplot2’s hue palette


bw
white panel with a dark border and light grid


linedraw
white panel with a black border and thin black grid lines


minimal
light grid, no border, and no axis lines


classic
axis lines and no grid


light
light gray border and grid


dark
dark background


void
no axes or grid



baseSize: scales every font size, with ggplot2’s proportions. Themes are written into the specification as Vega-Lite config, so HTML and static exports look the same.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point()
    ->theme('gray', baseSize: 12);

The individual options are:

font, textColor, and baseSize
legendPosition (right, left, top, bottom, or none), legendDirection (horizontal or vertical), and legendTitle: false
background, panelBackground, and panelBorder
grid, gridColor, axisLine, and ticks
xLabelAngle and yLabelAngle, which turn axis labels anticlockwise as element_text(angle =) does
titleAnchor and padding
captionSize, captionColor, and captionAnchor, which style labs(caption:)

config: accepts raw Vega-Lite config, merged last. Calls without a preset build on the current theme.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point()
    ->theme('minimal', legendPosition: 'bottom', font: 'Georgia, serif', config: ['axis' => ['labelColor' => '#666666']])
    ->labs(title: 'A minimal theme with the legend below');

A page can also choose a theme at render time. The vega-embed option theme accepts the vega-themes names, and phiz adds 'auto', which follows the reader’s light or dark mode preference:
$plot->embed(['theme' => 'auto']);

title: Scales, coordinates, and labels
text:
scaleX(), scaleY(), scaleColor(), scaleFill(), scaleSize(), scaleShape(), scaleOpacity(), and scaleLinetype() configure the scale and guide for one aesthetic. Successive calls for the same aesthetic merge. The common options:







Option
Sets




type
the scale type, such as log, sqrt, time, or quantize


domain, range
the input and output ranges


scheme
a Vega color scheme, such as viridis or set2


values
a manual palette: a level-to-value map, or a list in level order


name, breaks, format
the guide’s title, tick or legend values, and d3 format


labels
a label formatter, a value-to-label map, labels for breaks, or a Vega expression


guide: false
hides the axis or legend



The Scales and guides API lists every option.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::economics())
    ->aes(x: 'pop', y: 'pce')
    ->point(alpha: 0.4)
    ->scaleY(type: 'log', breaks: [500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000], name: 'Personal consumption ($bn, log scale)')
    ->scaleX(format: '.3s', name: 'Population (thousands)');

use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point(size: 40)
    ->scaleColor(values: ['f' => '#1B9E77', 'r' => '#7570B3', '4' => '#D95F02'], name: 'Drive');

Continuous position scales fit the data as in ggplot2: points and lines do not force the axis to include zero. Plots with bars, areas, histograms, or densities keep zero, since their lengths are measured from it. zero: true restores Vega-Lite’s default for a single scale.
The functions in Phiz\ include ggplot2’s shortcuts. Each returns a closure for the pipe operator or apply():







Function
Scale




scale_x_log10(), scale_x_sqrt(), scale_x_reverse(), scale_x_date()
transformed and date position scales


scale_x_discrete(limits:, labels:)
discrete positions: limits orders and subsets the levels, labels renames them


scale_color_manual(values)
a level-to-color map, or colors in level order


scale_color_brewer(palette), scale_color_distiller(), scale_color_fermenter()
ColorBrewer palettes for discrete, continuous, and binned data


scale_color_viridis_d(), _c(), _b()
viridis with option (A magma to E cividis, H turbo), begin, end, and direction


scale_color_gradient(), scale_color_gradient2(), scale_color_gradientn()
two-color, diverging, and many-color gradients


scale_color_hue(h:, c:, l:, hStart:, direction:)
ggplot2’s hue palette with its options


scale_color_grey(start:, end:)
grays, as grey.colors()


scale_color_identity()
the data values are the colors, with no legend



Each scale_color_*() has a scale_fill_*() twin. The hue and grey palettes are computed for the number of levels in the data.


The label functions follow the scales package. Pass one as labels:.



Function
0.256
12500




label_percent()
25.6%
1250000%


label_comma()
0.256
12,500


label_dollar()
$0.256
$12,500


label_number(accuracy: 0.1, suffix: ' kg')
0.3 kg
12,500.0 kg


label_scientific()
2.56e-1
1.25e+4


label_date('%b %Y')
for dates




accuracy rounds (0.01 keeps two decimals, and the default trims trailing zeros), scale multiplies first, and prefix and suffix wrap the number. label_dollar(scale: 0.001, suffix: 'k') writes 12500 as $12.5k.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

use function Phiz\guide_axis;
use function Phiz\label_percent;
use function Phiz\scale_fill_viridis_d;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'class', fill: 'drv')
    ->bar(position: 'fill')
    ->scaleY(labels: label_percent(), name: 'Share of cars')
    ->apply(scale_fill_viridis_d(begin: 0.2, end: 0.8))
    ->guides(x: guide_axis(angle: 45))
    ->labs(x: null, fill: 'Drive');




guides() sets the axis or legend for each aesthetic, as ggplot2’s guides() does. 'none' hides one. guide_axis(angle:) turns axis labels, guide_legend(title:, ncol:, direction:) arranges a legend, and guide_colorbar(barwidth:, barheight:) sizes a color bar. Any other Vega-Lite axis or legend property can be passed as a named argument.
guide_axis(cap: true) draws the axis line only from the first break to the last, as ggplot2’s guide_axis(cap = "both") does. With a padded domain, such as scaleX(domain: [-4, 104], breaks: [0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100]), the line stops at 0 and 100 and stands apart from the panel corners. It needs breaks or a domain. Faceted plots do not support it, because the line would be drawn in every panel.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

use function Phiz\scale_color_grey;
use function Phiz\scale_x_discrete;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'drv', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->boxplot()
    ->apply(scale_x_discrete(limits: ['f', 'r', '4'], labels: ['f' => 'Front', 'r' => 'Rear', '4' => '4WD']))
    ->apply(scale_color_grey())
    ->guides(color: 'none')
    ->labs(x: 'Drive', y: 'Highway mpg')
    ->theme('bw');

title: Scales, coordinates, and labels
Scales, coordinates, and labels
text:
Labels
labs() sets the title, subtitle, caption, and the title for any aesthetic. A null title removes it. Titles for position aesthetics apply to everything drawn on that axis, including ranges and reference lines. A facet field’s name sets its panel header title.
$plot->labs(
    title: 'Fuel economy',
    subtitle: 'EPA data, 1999 and 2008',
    x: 'Displacement (L)',
    y: 'Highway mpg',
    color: 'Drive',
);
The caption sits below the plot, right-aligned and smaller than the axis titles, as in ggplot2. theme(captionSize:, captionColor:, captionAnchor:) changes its size, color, and alignment (start, middle, or end).
With both a title and a caption, size() sets the plot area alone, and the titles, axes, and caption are added around it. (phiz emits such a plot as a Vega-Lite vconcat, which autosize fit does not apply to.)

title: API reference
text: The reference is generated from the public signatures and docblocks in src/, and is split into pages by topic. Each page starts with an index of its methods and functions, and every entry has its own anchor.

title: API reference
text:
Conventions
Every Plot method that adds or changes something returns a new Plot, and the plot it was called on is unchanged.
Most functions in the Phiz\ namespace return a closure that applies the Plot method of the same name, for PHP 8.5’s pipe operator and for apply(). They take the same arguments as that method. Each method’s entry lists the functions that wrap it. A function with arguments of its own, such as scale_color_manual(), also has an entry.

title: API reference
text:
Aesthetics
aes() and every geom’s aes argument accept these names: x, y, xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, xend, yend, color (or colour), fill, size, shape, opacity (or alpha), linetype, group, detail, tooltip, label (or text), order, href, theta, radius, xintercept, yintercept, sample, key, and description.

title: API reference
text:
Exceptions

InvalidArgumentException for input phiz cannot use, such as an unknown aesthetic, scale type, theme, or legend position, a geom without an aesthetic it needs, data that is neither rows nor columns, or a plot with no layers. The message names the problem.
Phiz\Exceptions\VlConvertNotFound when static export cannot find the vl-convert binary.
Phiz\Exceptions\ExportFailed when vl-convert fails, times out, or writes nothing, or when a file cannot be written.

Both export exceptions implement Phiz\Exceptions\PhizException.

title: Statistics API
text:
These functions turn model results from phit and draws from CmdStanPHP into plots. Each returns an ordinary Plot or Compose, which any plot method can restyle. Statistics describes the fit arrays they accept and shows each one.
Functions: coefplot() · residual_plot() · qq_plot() · fitted_plot() · scale_location_plot() · diagnostic_plots() · effect_plot() · predictions() · interval_plot() · marginal_means() · random_effects_plot()

coefplot()
coefplot(array $fits, mixed ...$options): Plot
Coefficient plot of one fit, or of several keyed by label (dodged side by side).


residual_plot()
residual_plot(array $fit): Plot
Residuals against fitted values, with a reference line at zero.


qq_plot()
qq_plot(array $fitOrValues, bool $standardize = false): Plot
A normal QQ plot of a fit’s residuals, or of a list of values; standardize scales them first.


fitted_plot()
fitted_plot(array $fit, ?array $observed = null): Plot
Observed against fitted values, with the identity line; observed defaults to fitted plus residuals.


scale_location_plot()
scale_location_plot(array $fit): Plot
The square root of the absolute residuals divided by sigma, against fitted values, as R’s plot(fit, 3).


diagnostic_plots()
diagnostic_plots(array $fit, mixed ...$options): Compose
residual_plot(), qq_plot(), scale_location_plot(), and fitted_plot() in a two-by-two grid.


effect_plot()
effect_plot(array $fit, mixed $data, string $x, mixed ...$options): Plot
Predicted values with confidence bands as x varies (by levels of $by), other variables held at typical values.


predictions()
predictions(array $fit, array $grid, mixed ...$options): array
The predicted rows behind effect_plot() for a grid of rows, without plotting them: each row with estimate, lower, upper, and std_error.


interval_plot()
interval_plot(array $draws, mixed ...$options): Plot
Posterior intervals from draws columns or a summary, as bayesplot’s mcmc_intervals.


marginal_means()
marginal_means(array $fit, mixed $data, string $factor, mixed ...$options): Plot
Estimated marginal means of a factor with confidence intervals, as emmeans.


random_effects_plot()
random_effects_plot(array $fit, mixed $data = null, mixed ...$options): Plot
A caterpillar plot of a mixed model’s random effects with conditional intervals, as lme4’s dotplot(ranef()).

title: Plots and data API
text:
A plot starts with Plot::of() or ggplot(), which take the data and optional mappings. The data can be rows, columns, a phibble table, a Laravel collection, or a Data source. Data and fields explains the forms data can take, and Large data explains when to bin in PHP with Bin.

Bin

Bin::histogram()
Bin::histogram(
    mixed $source,
    string $x,
    int $bins = 30,
    int|float|null $binwidth = null,
    int|float|null $boundary = null,
    ?array $limits = null,
    array $groups = [],
): array
Equal-width bins of x: rows with x0, x1, count, and density (count / (n * width)), per group.


Bin::grid()
Bin::grid(
    mixed $source,
    string $x,
    string $y,
    array|int $bins = 30,
    ?array $xlim = null,
    ?array $ylim = null,
    array $groups = [],
): array
Counts in a grid of x-by-y rectangles: rows with x_start, x_end, y_start, y_end (named after the fields) and count. Empty cells are omitted.


Bin::hex()
Bin::hex(
    mixed $source,
    string $x,
    string $y,
    int $bins = 30,
    ?array $xlim = null,
    ?array $ylim = null,
    float $aspect = 1.0,
    array $groups = [],
): array
Counts in a hexagonal grid, as ggplot2’s geom_hex: rows with the hexagon centers (under the x and y names) and count. bins hexagons span the x range; aspect (height / width of the panel in pixels) keeps them regular on screen.


Bin::lttb()
Bin::lttb(
    array $rows,
    string $x,
    string $y,
    int $threshold = 1000,
    array $groups = [],
): array
Downsamples a line to about $threshold points with Largest-Triangle-Three-Buckets, which keeps the visual shape (peaks and troughs). Rows are sorted by x; groups are downsampled separately.


Bin::sample()
Bin::sample(mixed $source, int $n, int $seed = 1): array
A uniform random sample of n rows (reservoir sampling, one pass), reproducible with a seed.


Bin::range()

The [min, max] of a numeric field, padded when every value is equal.

The values of the named fields, one list per record.

->coordFlip(bool $flip = true): Plot
Swaps the x and y channels, so mappings stay as written while the plot turns sideways.
Function: coord_flip().


coordPolar()
->coordPolar(
    string $theta = 'x',
    float $start = 0.0,
    int $direction = 1,
    int|float $innerRadius = 0,
): Plot
Polar coordinates for bar() and col() layers, as ggplot2’s coord_polar. theta: ‘y’ turns stacked bars into a pie (map x to a constant, or leave it out; innerRadius in pixels makes a donut), and ‘x’ turns bars over a discrete x into a rose of equal angles with radius y. start rotates the first slice clockwise from twelve o’clock, in radians; direction -1 runs anticlockwise.
Function: coord_polar().


coordFixed()
->coordFixed(int|float $ratio = 1): Plot
A fixed aspect ratio, as ggplot2’s coord_fixed: one unit of y takes ratio times the length of one unit of x. The panel’s height follows from the width (300 pixels unless set) and the data ranges, which are kept exact.
Functions: coord_fixed(), coord_equal().


coordCartesian()
->coordCartesian(?array $xlim = null, ?array $ylim = null): Plot
Zooms to fixed domains, clipping marks outside them.
Function: coord_cartesian().


facetWrap()
->facetWrap(
    array|string $facets,
    ?int $ncol = null,
    ?int $nrow = null,
    string $scales = 'fixed',
    array|string $labeller = 'value',
    array $header = [],
): Plot
Small multiples wrapped into rows. scales: fixed, free, free_x, free_y. With several fields the panels are their combinations. labeller: ‘both’ labels panels “field: value”, as ggplot2’s label_both.
Function: facet_wrap().


facetGrid()
->facetGrid(
    ?string $rows = null,
    ?string $cols = null,
    string $scales = 'fixed',
    array|string $labeller = 'value',
    array $header = [],
): Plot
A grid of panels by rows and/or cols fields.
Function: facet_grid().

title: Gallery
text: Each chart below is drawn from the code under it. The code uses the bundled datasets, loaded as $mpg = Datasets::mpg(), $mtcars = Datasets::mtcars(), $economics = Datasets::economics(), and $faithful = Datasets::faithful(). The statistics examples use a linear model fit and posterior draws defined at the top of examples/catalog.php, which holds every example.

title: Gallery
text:
Basics

Scatterplot
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'class')
    ->point()
    ->labs(
        x: 'Engine displacement (L)',
        y: 'Highway mpg',
        color: 'Class',
    );


Linear fit with confidence band
One least-squares line and 95% confidence band per group, computed in PHP.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point(alpha: 0.5)
    ->smooth(method: 'lm')
    ->labs(
        x: 'Displacement (L)',
        y: 'Highway mpg',
        color: 'Drive',
    );


With ggplot2-style functions
ggplot2-style functions compose with apply(), or with the pipe operator on PHP 8.5.
Vega-Lite specification
ggplot($mpg, aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy'))->apply(
    geom_point(alpha: 0.4),
    geom_smooth(span: 0.5),
    labs(
        title: 'Loess smooth',
        x: 'Displacement (L)',
        y: 'Highway mpg',
    ),
    theme_minimal(),
);


Time series
ISO dates are read as temporal fields.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($economics)
    ->aes(x: 'date', y: 'unemploy')
    ->line(color: '#1F77B4')
    ->labs(
        title: 'US unemployment',
        x: null,
        y: 'Unemployed (thousands)',
    );


Stacked area
Made-up monthly orders by channel. Areas stack by fill, so the top edge is the total.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of(array_merge(...array_map(
    fn ($month) => [
        ['month' => $month, 'channel' => 'Web',
            'orders' => 400 + 12 * $month],
        ['month' => $month, 'channel' => 'App',
            'orders' => 150 + 20 * $month],
        ['month' => $month, 'channel' => 'Store',
            'orders' => 300 - 6 * $month],
    ],
    range(1, 24),
)))
    ->aes(x: 'month', y: 'orders', fill: 'channel')
    ->area(alpha: 0.8)
    ->labs(x: 'Month', y: 'Orders', fill: 'Channel');


Labels
nudgeY moves each label above its point.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of(array_slice($mtcars, 0, 12))
    ->aes(x: 'wt', y: 'mpg', label: 'model')
    ->point()
    ->text(nudgeY: 8, size: 9)
    ->labs(x: 'Weight (1000 lbs)', y: 'mpg');

title: Gallery
text:
Distributions

Histogram
bins sets the maximum number of bins.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($faithful)
    ->aes(x: 'waiting')
    ->histogram(bins: 30, fill: '#4C78A8')
    ->labs(x: 'Minutes between eruptions', y: 'Count');


Histogram with density
density: true scales the bars to unit area, so a density curve can overlay them.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($faithful)
    ->aes(x: 'eruptions')
    ->histogram(
        binwidth: 0.25,
        density: true,
        fill: '#DDDDDD',
        color: '#999999',
    )
    ->density(color: '#D62728', linewidth: 2)
    ->labs(x: 'Eruption length (minutes)');


Density by group
Computed in the browser by Vega-Lite’s density transform.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'hwy', fill: 'drv')
    ->density(alpha: 0.4)
    ->labs(x: 'Highway mpg', fill: 'Drive');


Boxplots
Tukey boxplots, flipped for readable labels.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class', y: 'hwy', fill: 'class')
    ->boxplot()
    ->coordFlip()
    ->scaleFill(guide: false)
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Highway mpg');


Violins with boxplots
In ggplot2’s gray theme and hue palette.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class', y: 'hwy', fill: 'class')
    ->violin(alpha: 0.6)
    ->boxplot(width: 8, outliers: false)
    ->scaleFill(guide: false)
    ->theme('gray')
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Highway mpg');


Jittered strip plot
Each point moves randomly by up to 0.3 of a band.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: factor('cyl'), y: 'hwy', color: factor('cyl'))
    ->jitter(width: 0.3, alpha: 0.6)
    ->labs(x: 'Cylinders', y: 'Highway mpg')
    ->scaleColor(guide: false);


Empirical CDF
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'cty', color: 'drv')
    ->ecdf()
    ->labs(
        x: 'City mpg',
        y: 'Proportion ≤ x',
        color: 'Drive',
    );


QQ plot
Sample quantiles against normal quantiles, with the line through the quartiles.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(sample: 'hwy')
    ->qq(alpha: 0.6)
    ->qqLine(color: '#D62728');


2D density
Density bands computed in PHP as MASS::kde2d does, with the points on top.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($faithful)
    ->aes(x: 'eruptions', y: 'waiting')
    ->density2dFilled()
    ->point(size: 6, color: 'white', alpha: 0.5)
    ->labs(
        x: 'Eruption (minutes)',
        y: 'Waiting (minutes)',
        fill: 'density',
    );


Confidence ellipses
Multivariate t ellipses per group, as stat_ellipse() draws by default.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point(alpha: 0.5)
    ->ellipse()
    ->labs(
        x: 'Displacement (L)',
        y: 'Highway mpg',
        color: 'Drive',
    );

title: Gallery
text:
Counts

Bar chart of counts
bar() counts rows when y is unmapped.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class')
    ->bar(fill: '#4C78A8')
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Cars');


Dodged bars
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class', fill: 'drv')
    ->bar(position: 'dodge')
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Cars', fill: 'Drive');


Proportions
position: fill stacks each bar to 100%.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class', fill: 'drv')
    ->bar(position: 'fill')
    ->scaleY(format: '%')
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Share of cars', fill: 'Drive');


Bars of values
col() draws the y values, here an aggregate.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'manufacturer', y: 'mean(hwy)')
    ->col(fill: '#72B7B2')
    ->coordFlip()
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Mean highway mpg');


Heatmap
Each tile is filled by the mean of its rows.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class', y: factor('cyl'), fill: 'mean(hwy)')
    ->tile(color: 'white')
    ->scaleFill(scheme: 'viridis')
    ->labs(x: null, y: 'Cylinders', fill: 'Mean hwy');


2D histogram
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($faithful)
    ->aes(x: 'eruptions', y: 'waiting')
    ->bin2d(bins: 20)
    ->scaleFill(scheme: 'blues');


Donut
innerRadius cuts out the center of a pie.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(fill: 'drv')
    ->pie(innerRadius: 50)
    ->labs(fill: 'Drive');


Polar bars
coordPolar() turns bars into a rose.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'class', fill: 'class')
    ->bar()
    ->coordPolar()
    ->labs(fill: null);


Annotations
annotate() adds shaded ranges, segments, and text.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'cty', y: 'hwy')
    ->annotate(
        'rect',
        xmin: 15, xmax: 20, ymin: -INF, ymax: INF,
        fill: 'orange', alpha: 0.2,
    )
    ->count(alpha: 0.6)
    ->annotate(
        'text',
        x: 30, y: 23, label: 'Most efficient',
        color: '#D62728',
    )
    ->labs(x: 'City mpg', y: 'Highway mpg');

title: Gallery
text:
Facets

Small multiples
facetWrap() with a fitted line in every panel.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy')
    ->point(alpha: 0.5)
    ->smooth(method: 'lm')
    ->facetWrap('class', ncol: 4)
    ->size(150, 120);


Grid of panels
Rows by drive, columns by year.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'cty', y: 'hwy')
    ->point(alpha: 0.5)
    ->abline(0, 1, linetype: 'dashed', color: '#888888')
    ->facetGrid(rows: 'drv', cols: 'year')
    ->size(270, 140);


Side by side
Compose::beside() lays plots out like patchwork.
Vega-Lite specification
Compose::beside(
    Plot::of($faithful)
        ->aes(x: 'eruptions', y: 'waiting')
        ->point(alpha: 0.5)
        ->size(420, 260),
    Plot::of($faithful)
        ->aes(x: 'waiting')
        ->histogram(bins: 20)
        ->coordFlip()
        ->size(180, 260),
)->title('Old Faithful');

title: Gallery
text:
Scales and themes

Log scale
scaleX(type: ‘log’) with chosen breaks.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($economics)
    ->aes(x: 'pce', y: 'psavert')
    ->point(alpha: 0.4)
    ->scaleX(
        type: 'log',
        breaks: [500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000],
        name: 'Personal consumption ($bn, log)',
    )
    ->labs(y: 'Savings rate (%)');


Manual colors
A map from each level to its color.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point()
    ->scaleColor(
        values: [
            '4' => '#D95F02',
            'f' => '#1B9E77',
            'r' => '#7570B3',
        ],
        name: 'Drive',
    );


Continuous color
A viridis gradient for a numeric field.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'cty')
    ->point(size: 50)
    ->scaleColor(scheme: 'viridis');


theme(“gray”)
ggplot2’s default look.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point()
    ->theme('gray');


theme(“classic”, baseSize: 13)
Axis lines, no grid, larger text.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy')
    ->point()
    ->theme('classic', baseSize: 13);


theme(“dark”)
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($economics)
    ->aes(x: 'date', y: 'psavert')
    ->line(color: '#F58518')
    ->theme('dark');

title: Gallery
text:
Interaction

Tooltips, pan and zoom
Hover for values. Drag to pan and scroll to zoom.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'class')
    ->point()
    ->tooltip([
        'manufacturer', 'model', 'year', 'displ', 'hwy',
    ])
    ->interactive();


Linked brushing
Brush the scatterplot to filter the bars.
Vega-Lite specification
Compose::stack(
    Plot::of($mpg)
        ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
        ->point()
        ->brush(encodings: ['x', 'y'])
        ->size(600, 240),
    Plot::of($mpg)
        ->aes(x: 'class')
        ->bar(filter: ['param' => 'brush'])
        ->size(600, 140),
);


Legend highlight
Click a legend entry. Shift-click selects several.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point(size: 40)
    ->highlight();


Slider-driven reference line
The slider moves the rule and recolors the points.
Vega-Lite specification
Plot::of($mpg)
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy')
    ->slider('cutoff', 15, 40, 1, 30, 'Highway mpg cutoff')
    ->point(filter: 'datum.hwy >= cutoff', color: '#D62728')
    ->point(filter: 'datum.hwy < cutoff', color: '#BBBBBB')
    ->hline(expr('cutoff'), linetype: 'dashed');

title: Save a chart to a file
text:
Result
The SVG file:

The file extension picks the format: html (or htm), json for the Vega-Lite specification, svg, png, jpg (or jpeg), or pdf.

HTML needs a network connection. The page loads vega, vega-lite, and vega-embed from the jsDelivr CDN and draws the chart in the browser. Assets::inline() embeds the libraries for offline use.
Images need vl-convert. The vl-convert binary renders SVG, PNG, JPG, and PDF without a browser. Without it, save() throws VlConvertNotFound (Installing vl-convert).
Images are static. Tooltips and other interaction work only in the HTML file.
Image size. An image has no page width to fill, so size(640, 360) sets its plot area in pixels. Without it, Vega-Lite’s default size applies.
Reproducible SVG. With the same vl-convert version, the same specification gives the same SVG bytes on every run, except for unseeded jitter (Reproducible SVG).

See also: save() · size() · html() · svg() · png() · pdf() · Rendering

title: Compare groups with facets
Compare groups with facets
text:
Result
Vega-Lite specification

Shared scales. By default every panel has the same axis ranges, so positions compare across panels.
Free scales. scales: 'free', 'free_x', or 'free_y' gives each panel its own ranges. Positions then no longer compare across panels.
Mixed effects. Heavier cars also tend to have more cylinders. Each panel shows the weight and economy association among cars with the same cylinder count.
Small groups. The panels hold 11, 7, and 14 cars, so a trend within one panel is a rough description.

title: Design and compatibility
text:
phiz does not draw graphics. It translates a ggplot2-style description into a Vega-Lite specification. Vega-Lite then resolves scales, lays out facets and legends, runs transforms, handles interaction, and renders to canvas or SVG. The PHP side stays small, and plots behave the same in the browser and in static export.
Statistics run as Vega-Lite transforms where Vega-Lite has them: bins, densities with the default bandwidth, aggregates, quantiles, and window functions. phiz computes a statistic in PHP when Vega-Lite has no equivalent, or when matching R needs it:

smooth() fits and their confidence bands (loess up to 3,000 rows, lm, quad, and poly)
violin densities, and the R bw.nrd0 bandwidth behind density(adjust:)
2D densities, contours, and filled contours
ellipse() and the summaries of summary()
hex(), and bin2d() and histogram() above Config::$serverRows rows
line(downsample:)
curve() evaluations of PHP functions
the statistics helpers’ intervals and predictions

title: Data and fields
text:
Field types
Vega-Lite needs a measurement type for every mapped field. phiz infers it from inline data:

quantitative, when every non-null value is an integer or a float
temporal, when every value is an ISO date or date-time string
nominal, otherwise

A numeric code such as a cylinder count is quantitative by this rule. It gets a continuous color scale and gradient legend unless you mark it as categorical. Field shorthand sets the type explicitly with a suffix: :Q (quantitative), :N (nominal), :O (ordinal), or :T (temporal). factor('cyl') is the equivalent of R’s factor(cyl), and its levels: argument sets the order.
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;

use function Phiz\factor;

$plot = Plot::of(Datasets::mtcars())
    ->aes(x: 'wt', y: 'mpg', color: factor('cyl'), shape: 'am:N')
    ->point(size: 60)
    ->labs(color: 'Cylinders', shape: 'Manual');

URL data cannot be inspected in PHP, so phiz assumes quantitative positions and nominal groupings. Use shorthand types for anything else.

title: Data and fields

Field definitions
field() builds a Field with any Vega-Lite field-definition property, such as field('date', timeUnit: 'month', title: 'Month') or field('term', sort: ['b', 'a', 'c']). A raw array is also accepted for any aesthetic and is used as given.

title: Layer points and a fitted line
text:
Result
Vega-Lite specification

Inheritance. Both layers use the data and the x and y mappings given to ggplot(). A layer’s own mappings or data override them.
The band. The band is a 95% confidence interval for the mean response, not a prediction interval for individual cars.
R parity. phiz computes the line and the band in PHP. They match R’s predict(fit, interval = "confidence").
Straight line. The points rise again at the largest displacements, which a straight line cannot follow. The default method, loess, fits a local curve (Fitted curves).
Association. Cars with larger engines tend to have lower highway economy in this data. The line describes that association, not the effect of changing a car’s engine.

In R: ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) + geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + geom_smooth(method = "lm").

title: Coming from ggplot2
text:
Differences

Sizes. Point size is an area in square pixels, as in Vega-Lite, rather than a diameter in millimeters. The default is 30. linewidth is in pixels.
Bins. bins: is a maximum, and Vega-Lite rounds the boundaries. Use binwidth: and boundary: for exact bins.
Limits. xlim() and ylim() zoom without removing data. ggplot2 removes the data outside the limits, which changes statistics computed from it.
Densities. The default bandwidth is Vega-Lite’s. adjust: multiplies R’s bw.nrd0, so adjust: 1 reproduces ggplot2’s default.
Smoothers. Loess, lm, quad, and poly fits and their bands are computed in PHP. Loess follows R’s loess(surface = "direct"), while ggplot2 interpolates the loess surface, so its curve can differ slightly. Above 3,000 rows, loess falls back to Vega-Lite’s transform without a band, where ggplot2 switches to a GAM. There is no gam method.
Colors. Categorical colors come from Vega-Lite’s palette by default. theme('gray') switches to ggplot2’s hue_pal() colors, computed for the number of levels. scaleColor(values:) or scheme: sets them explicitly.
Panels. A discrete axis is 300 pixels by default, the same as a continuous axis, and grows by 20 pixels per level beyond 15 levels.
Violins. violin() draws each violin as a Vega-Lite trail, whose ends are rounded. There is no draw_quantiles option; layer a boxplot() instead.
Polar coordinates. coordPolar() draws bars, columns, and arcs. Vega-Lite has no polar form for lines, points, or areas, so radar charts are not available.
Not available. There is no sec_axis(), no geom_dotplot(), and no geom_quantile(). Use raw() or layer() for any Vega-Lite feature phiz does not wrap.

title: Coming from ggplot2
text:
Additions
phiz also has features that ggplot2 leaves to other packages:

tooltips, pan and zoom, brushing, legend highlighting, and sliders (see Interaction)
linked views across compositions
the statistics helpers for phit fits and CmdStanPHP draws (see Statistics)
Vega-Lite aggregates and time units in field shorthand, such as 'mean(hwy)' and 'year(date):O'

title: Interaction
text: Interaction in phiz is expressed as Vega-Lite parameters, so it works in any page that renders the specification. Static exports draw the initial state.

Interaction
Interaction
Large data
text: phiz embeds inline data in the specification, and the browser keeps every row in memory to draw it. Summarize large data in PHP before it reaches the page.

title: Large data
text:
Sizes to expect
These ranges are rough guidance, not measurements. The limits depend on the mark type, the number of layers and interactions, the browser, and the device. Only the warning threshold is set by phiz.







Rows embedded
Typical effect




up to a few thousand
draws quickly, with responsive interaction


5,000 to 20,000
draws, but brushing and tooltips can lag


above 20,000
phiz raises a warning, and the page grows by megabytes


millions
summarize in PHP or in the database



Config::$warnRows sets the warning threshold (20,000 by default, or null to turn it off). In Laravel it is config('phiz.warn_rows'). The warning is an E_USER_WARNING that names the alternatives below.

title: Large data
Large data
text:
Tables stay columnar
A phibble table or an array of columns is kept as given. The binning geoms read it column by column, and rows are built only if the specification embeds them.

title: Large data
Large data
text:
The Bin helpers
The Bin class exposes the same computations for data you summarize yourself. Each helper returns a short list of rows. The helpers read phibble tables, column arrays, row lists, or any iterable of rows. A generator streams in one pass when the limits are given.







Helper
Returns rows of




Bin::histogram($source, 'price', bins: 50)
price_start, price_end, count, density


Bin::grid($source, 'x', 'y', bins: [40, 30])
x_start, x_end, y_start, y_end, count


Bin::hex($source, 'x', 'y', bins: 30, aspect: 0.75)
hexagon centers and count


Bin::lttb($rows, 'time', 'value', threshold: 1000)
the rows LTTB keeps


Bin::sample($source, 5000, seed: 1)
a reproducible uniform sample



use Phiz\Bin;

// One pass over a database cursor, with known limits:
$bins = Bin::grid(
    Car::query()->cursor(),
    'weight',
    'mpg',
    bins: 40,
    xlim: [1500, 5500],
    ylim: [5, 50],
);

Plot::of($bins)->rect(aes(
    xmin: 'weight_start',
    xmax: 'weight_end',
    ymin: 'mpg_start',
    ymax: 'mpg_end',
    fill: 'count',
));

title: Large data
text:
Other approaches

Summarize first. phplyr’s group_by() and summarize(), or a SQL GROUP BY, usually answers the question with far fewer rows. Dashboards with Livewire shows charts built from summaries.
Load from a URL. Data::url('/data/points.csv') lets the browser fetch the file, so the page itself stays small. The browser still holds every row, so this helps page size, not drawing speed.
Sample. Bin::sample() keeps a uniform random subset when a scatterplot of individual points matters more than exact counts.

toArray() returns the Vega-Lite specification and toJson() encodes it. Plots also implement JsonSerializable. The specification declares the Vega-Lite 6 schema.
These escape hatches reach the parts of Vega-Lite that phiz does not wrap:

raw([...]) deep-merges arbitrary Vega-Lite into the top level. Nested objects merge, and lists and scalars replace.
transform(...) adds Vega-Lite transforms that run before every layer.
layer([...]) adds a raw Vega-Lite layer.
param() and select() add raw parameters.

In the browser
embed() returns a chart container followed by the script tags, and html() returns a complete page. Both take vega-embed options, such as ['actions' => false] or ['renderer' => 'svg'].
The container holds the specification in a data-phiz attribute. phiz’s loader script draws every such container with vega-embed and redraws it when the attribute changes, so the same markup works in static pages, Blade views, and Livewire components.

title: Rendering
text:
Static export
svg(), png(), pdf(), and save() with an image extension run the vl-convert binary, which renders without a browser.
$plot->save('figure.svg');
$plot->save('figure.png', scale: 3);
file_put_contents('figure.pdf', $plot->pdf());

Finding the binary. phiz checks the PHIZ_VL_CONVERT and VL_CONVERT environment variables, then PATH. A missing binary throws Phiz\Exceptions\VlConvertNotFound with installation instructions.
Options. new Export(binary:, timeout:, fontDir:) sets the binary path, the timeout, and an extra font directory.


Installing vl-convert
vl-convert has no Homebrew formula or apt package. Each release ships a self-contained binary for macOS (osx-arm64, osx-64) and Linux (linux-64, linux-aarch64). The Linux binaries link only against glibc and zlib, so they run on a bare Ubuntu image with no fonts or other packages installed. On Ubuntu the install is:
curl -sSLo /tmp/vl-convert.zip https://github.com/vega/vl-convert/releases/download/v1.9.0/vl-convert_linux-64.zip
sudo unzip -j -o /tmp/vl-convert.zip bin/vl-convert -d /usr/local/bin
vl-convert --version
On macOS, download vl-convert_osx-arm64.zip from the same release and unzip it the same way. The macOS binary has only an ad hoc signature. A copy fetched with curl or gh release download is not quarantined and runs directly. If a browser download is quarantined, xattr -d com.apple.quarantine vl-convert clears the flag. Put the binary in a directory on PATH, or point PHIZ_VL_CONVERT at it.


Reproducible SVG

Repeated runs. With the same vl-convert version, the same specification gives the same SVG bytes on every run. Unseeded jitter is the exception: without seed:, jitter() uses Vega’s random(). With seed:, the offsets are part of the specification.
Fonts. vl-convert measures sans-serif text with its bundled Liberation Sans, so the layout does not depend on the fonts installed on the machine. The SVG keeps its text as <text font-family="sans-serif">, so the viewer’s browser chooses the displayed font. A theme that names another font, or an export with fontDir:, makes the layout depend on the fonts vl-convert can find.
Across machines. The visual tests render on macOS and on Linux in CI and compare both with the same PNG baselines, within a pixel tolerance.
Committed figures change when the specification, the vl-convert version, or its Vega-Lite version changes. Pin the vl-convert version wherever figures are generated.

title: Statistics
text: The statistics helpers turn model results into ordinary plots, which any Plot method can restyle. They read the arrays that phit returns from its extension or its PHP polyfill, and the draws that CmdStanPHP returns. The fits on this page are saved in docs/examples/fits/, from the mtcars and mpg data.

Requirements
Plotting a fit array needs no extension. Phit\model_matrix(), from the phit extension or phpstats/phit-polyfill, is needed only where noted below. Without it, those calls throw an InvalidArgumentException.

Link and response scales. GLM intervals are computed on the link scale and transformed to the response scale, so they can be asymmetric there.
Singular fits. When a mixed model’s variance is estimated at zero, or its random effects are perfectly correlated, random_effects_plot() says so in the subtitle. The intervals still follow lme4.
